classification.difficultyReason: Compare a parameter-dependent equation with an equivalent multiple to distinguish parallel and coincident lines.

content.prompt: The equations of two lines are $x+2y=7$ and $2x+4y=k$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: For what values of $k$ will the two lines not intersect?

answer.worked:
Writing each equation in gradient–intercept form gives
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-\frac12x+\frac72\\y&=-\frac12x+\frac{k}{4}.\end{aligned}$$
The gradients are equal. The lines do not intersect when their intercepts differ:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{k}{4}&\ne\frac72\\k&\ne14.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: For what values of $k$ will the two lines intersect?

answer.worked:
The gradients are equal, so the lines can have common points only when their intercepts are equal:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{k}{4}&=\frac72\\k&=14.\end{aligned}$$
For this value, $2x+4y=14$ is twice $x+2y=7$, so the equations represent the same line.

children.label: c
children.prompt: For the values of $k$ found in part b, comment on the intersection of the lines.

answer.short: When $k=14$, the lines are the same and have infinitely many common points.
answer.worked: When $k=14$, dividing $2x+4y=14$ by $2$ gives $x+2y=7$. The equations are equivalent, so the lines coincide. Every point on this line is a common point; there are infinitely many solutions.
